title: RootCandidate finite-extreme metrics (f32::MAX) still win root selection (Rust + C parity gap)
description: Edge-review finding on 96ce (follow-up, beyond the bead's mirror-C scope): the non-finite sanitization (NaN/±inf -> worst-case) is done, but a finite extreme like f32::MAX passes is_finite() and its combined_score outranks all sane candidates under preference/stratum ties — a malformed-but-finite beacon metric still forces root selection. Affects BOTH rust (multi_instance.rs compare via Ord/total_cmp) and C (tdma_root_select.c, which sanitizes non-finite only). Fix direction: clamp the metric ranges to the plausible RF domain (RSSI in [-200, 0], SNR in [-40, 40] per the units doc) in both implementations' sanitize paths, with boundary pins; or treat |value| beyond physical bounds as non-finite. Cross-impl parity required (same clamp in both).
